non_blocking_notes: Performance: _materialize() rebuilds and re-joins the full packaged edge table (197,794 rows) on every public call, including pick(), which discards the edge frame and only needs vocabulary, and from_frame(), which builds a ~198k-entry key dict even for a one-row input. Measured in the worktree: find() ~1.9-3.0 s, pick() ~0.89 s per call. Caching was outside the plan's scope, but a memoized materialization is the obvious follow-up before this surface is used interactively.

test_pick_rejects_vocabulary_lists_atomically assigns before = base (the same object) and then asserts base == before and _keys(base) == before_keys. Both are tautologies for an immutable object and would survive any mutation of pick(). The plan mandated this exact shape, and the real protection is the frozen-dataclass assertion in test 1, so it is not a defect in this change - but the assertion carries no regression value.

Two of the four exact error texts the plan fixes in section 2.4 are unasserted by any test: the unscoped "Station is not registered: 'does-not-exist'" and the multi-provider "Station is not registered for providers ('fr_hubeau', 'usgs_nwis'): 'does-not-exist'". I verified both manually against the head commit and they render exactly as specified, and section 5.3 did not ask for them - but the branch in UnknownStationError.__init__ that produces them is untested and free to drift.

_selection_from_edge_frame carries a mypy-style `# type: ignore[arg-type]` while the stated typecheck gate is `ty check src`. The suppression is at a genuine dynamic boundary (_Series(**row) from iter_rows(named=True)) and hides nothing, but the error code is not one ty emits; `# ty: ignore[...]` would be the checker-accurate spelling.

_normalize(()) collapses an empty sequence to "no filter", so pick(selection, product=[]) returns the whole input rather than an empty selection. The plan does not specify empty-sequence semantics; worth pinning explicitly before callers depend on either reading.

from_frame() additionally rejects identity columns that are present but relatively reordered, with the message "Selection frame identity columns are not in canonical order", and rejects non-Utf8 identity dtypes with its own message. Both follow from the plan's "at least these three columns in this order and with exact pl.Utf8 dtypes", but the texts are authored rather than quoted, so they are not covered by the plan's exact-message contract and are unasserted.
as_frame() uses dataclasses.asdict(), which recursively deep-copies each row; dataclasses.astuple or a direct attribute tuple would avoid that cost on large selections. Purely stylistic at this size.
summary:
APPROVE. The change delivers exactly the plan's contract and nothing else. The commit touches precisely the five write-set paths (src/rivretrieve/_internal/selection.py new, discovery.py, __init__.py, tests/test_selection.py new, tests/test_package.py), is a single conventional commit with subject 'feat: add immutable catalogue selections' and no body or attribution footer, leaves __version__ at 0.1.49 with no tag, and leaves pr-body.md untracked (git status --short is exactly '?? pr-body.md'). No pre-existing assertion was weakened or deleted: the only edited test is the mandated exact-public-name set in test_package.py, extended by exactly as_frame/find/from_frame/pick.

I re-ran the non-mutating gates against the named head in the worktree: `uv run pytest` gives 1637 passed, 2 skipped (the 1,622-passing baseline plus the 13 named tests and 2 extra parameterizations; the 2 skips are the pre-existing folium imports), `uv run ty check src` reports 'All checks passed!', `uv run ruff format --check` reports 164 files already formatted, `uv run ruff check` passes, and `git diff --check` exits 0. Acceptance criterion 3 reproduces the plan's stdout byte-for-byte: 0 / no_catalogue_edge / ('discharge_daily_mean', 'discharge_instantaneous', 'stage_instantaneous') / 831 / 24447.

Reading it as a maintainer, the semantics that carry risk hold up under probing beyond the tests. The edge rule filters availability != 'unavailable' before the joins and casts into the two-valued Enum, so 'unknown' survives as an edge and 'unavailable' cannot appear. Vocabulary is validated against the complete registered catalogue, in provider/product/station order, before any filtering, so pick(base, station='01646500') on a stage_daily_mean base returns not_in_selection rather than raising. Provider-scoped station identity is respected - find(station='01010000') keeps both fr_hubeau and usgs_nwis. _Selection.__post_init__ enforces the sorted-unique-keys and empty-reason-iff-empty invariants at construction, which is a stronger guarantee than the plan asked for and closes off malformed values from any internal path. I confirmed by direct in-place mutation (f[0,'unit'] = 'MUTATED') that writing to a returned frame leaves the selection and every subsequent as_frame() call untouched, and that the motivating use case - filter as_frame(selection) in Polars, then from_frame() it back - round-trips correctly with metadata rebuilt from the catalogue and caller columns discarded. The two exact error messages the required tests omit render exactly as the plan specifies. The PR body's four claims each map to real diff content.

The notes below are follow-ups and observations, not merge blockers. The substantive one is that every public call re-materializes the whole edge table, which makes pick() cost about a second for work that needs only vocabulary; caching was outside this step's scope.
